question: What personalised gene-editing treatment did baby KJ Muldoon receive, as reported in 2025?
text:
Baby KJ Muldoon received a **custom CRISPR base-editing therapy** designed to correct a specific mutation in his *CPS1* gene. The treatment used lipid nanoparticles to deliver the editor to his liver cells. KJ was born with severe carbamoyl phosphate synthetase 1 (CPS1) deficiency, a rare disorder that prevents the body from clearing toxic ammonia. ([beta.nih.gov](https://beta.nih.gov/news-events/nih-research-matters/infant-rare-disease-receives-customized-gene-therapy?utm_source=openai))

He received his first dose on February 25, 2025, at Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia, becoming the first person to receive a CRISPR therapy tailored to their individual mutation. ([chop.edu](https://www.chop.edu/news/worlds-first-patient-treated-personalized-crispr-gene-editing-therapy-childrens-hospital?utm_source=openai))
